28	//  * `LoopbackTransport` — the SINGLE-PROCESS, single-GPU loopback. The
29	//    "symmetric heap" is ONE device allocation of n_pes * stride floats; virtual
30	//    pe p's region is base + p*stride. All virtual PEs run in ONE grid (the CTAs
31	//    are partitioned into contiguous per-PE groups), so the cross-PE rendezvous
32	//    IS the existing GridBarrier over the whole grid. This is an HONEST
33	//    simulation: the TP math (shard GEMMs, partial publish, fixed-order
34	//    ascending-pe fp32 reduce) executes the IDENTICAL code path it executes on
35	//    NVSHMEM — the only thing swapped is (a) the symmetric-address translation
36	//    and (b) the rendezvous scope, which is precisely the transport abstraction.
37	//    It is NOT fake success: the loopback test (tests/hw/test_tp_loopback.py)
38	//    asserts bit-exact cross-virtual-rank identity + A/A/A + an exact-slice dW
39	//    check against the unsharded reference — failures fail loudly.
40	//
41	//  * `NvshmemTransport` — the REAL device-initiated NVSHMEM transport (design
42	//    §5.2). NVSHMEM IS NOT INSTALLED ON THIS BOX (verified 2026-06-12: no
43	//    headers/libs/pip/ldconfig hits), so this struct compiles ONLY under
44	//    -DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1 with the NVSHMEM toolkit on the include/link path. It is
45	//    NOT a stub that pretends to work: without the flag it does not exist, and
46	//    any attempt to instantiate the megakernel TP point with it is a loud
47	//    compile error pointing here. Wiring + validating it is the ONE genuinely
48	//    8×H100 task (design §7.5) — swap `LoopbackTransport` → `NvshmemTransport`
49	//    at the call sites and run the §5.4 go/no-go gate.
50	//
51	//  WHY offset-based symmetric addressing (not raw pointers): NVSHMEM's
52	//  symmetric heap guarantees the SAME offset is valid on every PE
53	//  (nvshmem_malloc returns symmetric addresses; nvshmem_ptr(sym, pe) translates
54	//  for NVLink load/store). The loopback reproduces exactly that property with
55	//  base + pe*stride. One addressing model ⇒ one math code path.
56	//
57	//  DETERMINISM (design §5.2, non-negotiable): the fixed-order all-reduce below
58	//  reads every PE's partial in ASCENDING pe order and accumulates fp32. The
59	//  summation order is STRUCTURAL (never timing-dependent), so the result is
60	//  bit-identical on every PE and across reruns — the cross-rank analogue of the
61	//  in-kernel ascending-CTA reduce that made the single-GPU path A/A/A.
62	//  A `nvshmem_float_sum_reduce` collective is deliberately NOT used (its
63	//  reduction order is unspecified) — on NVSHMEM the same ascending-pe loop runs
64	//  over nvshmem_ptr-translated peer pointers (NVLink direct load/store).
65	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
66	//
67	// HEADER-ONLY, self-contained: CUDA runtime + the GridBarrier substrate only.
68	// No torch, no NCCL. Compiles for sm_90a with plain nvcc.
69	// ============================================================================
70	
71	#include <cstdint>
72	#include <cuda_runtime.h>
73	
74	#include "csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh"   // GridBarrier (the in-kernel rendezvous)
75	
76	#if defined(SG_HAS_NVSHMEM)
77	// Real NVSHMEM headers — present ONLY when the toolkit is installed and the
78	// build opts in. NOT installed on the authoring box (see header comment).
79	#include <nvshmem.h>
80	#include <nvshmemx.h>
81	#endif

83	namespace sg { namespace fused { namespace sm90 { namespace tp {
84	
85	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
86	//  LoopbackTransport — single-process symmetric-heap simulation (the 1-GPU
87	//  honest test transport). See the swap-point doc above.
88	//
89	//  Host side: allocate ONE device buffer of `n_pes * stride_floats` floats and
90	//  pass (base, stride_floats, n_pes). Device side: each CTA derives its virtual
91	//  pe from its blockIdx (contiguous CTA groups per PE — `pe_of_cta`).
92	//  The rendezvous is the caller's whole-grid GridBarrier (all virtual PEs share
93	//  the grid), so `rendezvous()` simply forwards to bar.sync().
94	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
95	struct LoopbackTransport {
96	    float*  heap_base;       // [n_pes * stride_floats] device alloc
97	    int64_t stride_floats;   // per-PE symmetric region size
98	    int     n_pes_;          // TP degree being simulated
99	    int     my_pe_;          // this CTA-group's virtual rank
100	
101	    __device__ __forceinline__ int my_pe() const { return my_pe_; }
102	    __device__ __forceinline__ int n_pes() const { return n_pes_; }
103	
104	    // THIS pe's buffer at symmetric offset `off`.
105	    __device__ __forceinline__ float* local(int64_t off) const {
106	        return heap_base + (int64_t)my_pe_ * stride_floats + off;
107	    }
108	    // Peer pe's buffer at the SAME symmetric offset (ascending-pe reads in the
109	    // fixed-order reduce). On NVSHMEM this is nvshmem_ptr(sym, pe); here it is
110	    // the strided region — same contract, swapped translation.
111	    __device__ __forceinline__ const float* peer(int64_t off, int pe) const {
112	        return heap_base + (int64_t)pe * stride_floats + off;
113	    }
114	
115	    // Cross-PE rendezvous. Loopback: every virtual PE lives in THIS grid, so the
116	    // whole-grid GridBarrier IS the cross-PE barrier (publish partials → sync →
117	    // read peers → sync → reuse slots).
118	    __device__ __forceinline__ void rendezvous(const ::sg::fused::GridBarrier& bar) const {
119	        bar.sync();
120	    }
121	
122	    // Static CTA→PE partition helper: contiguous CTA groups (CTA c of nCTA, P
123	    // pes → pe = c / (nCTA/P); caller guarantees nCTA % P == 0, asserted in the
124	    // launchers). Contiguity keeps each virtual rank's tile traversal identical
125	    // to a real per-GPU grid (ascending tiles within the rank).
126	    __host__ __device__ __forceinline__ static int pe_of_cta(int cta, int nCTA, int P) {
127	        return cta / (nCTA / P);
128	    }
129	    __host__ __device__ __forceinline__ static int cta_within_pe(int cta, int nCTA, int P) {
130	        return cta % (nCTA / P);
131	    }
132	    __host__ __device__ __forceinline__ static int ctas_per_pe(int nCTA, int P) {
133	        return nCTA / P;
134	    }
135	};
136	
137	#if defined(SG_HAS_NVSHMEM)
138	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
139	//  NvshmemTransport — the REAL device-initiated transport (design §5.2).
140	//  COMPILED ONLY under -DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1 (NVSHMEM 3.7.0 IS installed:
141	//  NVSHMEM_HOME=/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/nvidia/nvshmem; the TU
142	//  that instantiates a kTPComm point must be built -rdc=true and device-linked
143	//  against libnvshmem_device_sm_90.bc — see /workspace/impl_diffs/tp_kernel.md
144	//  §6). The math code path is IDENTICAL to the loopback's; only the address
145	//  translation + the rendezvous scope differ:
146	//    * `heap_base` is an nvshmem_malloc'd SYMMETRIC allocation (same offset
147	//      valid on every PE) — a plain cudaMalloc pointer is NOT addressable via
148	//      nvshmem_ptr, so the TP slots MUST live on the symmetric heap the
149	//      launcher carves (tp_kernel.md §2/EDIT E). `tp_team_` is the TP-group
150	//      team (NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD when TP == world); `peer()` is called with the
151	//      TEAM-LOCAL pe and translated to the global pe for nvshmem_ptr.
152	//    * `peer()` translates via nvshmem_ptr (NVLink direct load/store — the
153	//      single-node 8×H100 case; a multi-node fabric would use nvshmem_get,
154	//      the documented extension point, NOT silently emulated);
155	//    * `rendezvous()` = in-GPU GridBarrier + nvshmem_quiet (drain THIS PE's
156	//      published partials so peers' NVLink loads see them) + ONE CTA running
157	//      the cross-GPU TEAM-scoped block barrier + GridBarrier again. The NVSHMEM
158	//      barrier is entered by exactly one CTA per GPU, NEVER concurrently with
159	//      the GridBarrier spin (the design's "two barrier systems must not
160	//      deadlock" rule, tp_nvshmem.md §1(3)).
161	//    * TEAM SCOPE: nvshmemx_barrier_block(tp_team_) joins ONLY the TP group, so
162	//      under a 4D mesh DP/PP replicas are not dragged into the TP barrier.
163	//      NVSHMEM 3.7.0 exposes nvshmemx_barrier_block (host/nvshmemx_coll_api.h:112),
164	//      so the tp_nvshmem.md §3.1 "version-dependent follow-up" is RESOLVED — no
165	//      whole-world fallback needed.
166	//  GO/NO-GO (§5.4): parity vs host-NCCL TP, A/A/A, MFU, ZeRO-3/DP composition.
167	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
168	struct NvshmemTransport {
169	    float*         heap_base;  // nvshmem_malloc'd symmetric base (LOCAL pointer)
170	    nvshmem_team_t tp_team_;   // the TP-group team (NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD if TP==world)
171	    int            n_pes_;     // TP group size  (nvshmem_team_n_pes(tp_team_))
172	    int            my_pe_;     // this GPU's pe-in-team (nvshmem_team_my_pe(tp_team_))
173	
174	    __device__ __forceinline__ int my_pe() const { return my_pe_; }
175	    __device__ __forceinline__ int n_pes() const { return n_pes_; }
176	
177	    __device__ __forceinline__ float* local(int64_t off) const {
178	        return heap_base + off;
179	    }
180	    __device__ __forceinline__ const float* peer(int64_t off, int pe_in_team) const {
181	        // peer() is called with the TEAM-LOCAL pe index (ascending 0..n_pes()-1,
182	        // the fixed reduce order); map it to the GLOBAL pe nvshmem_ptr needs.
183	        const int global_pe = nvshmem_team_translate_pe(tp_team_, pe_in_team,
184	                                                         NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD);
185	        return static_cast<const float*>(nvshmem_ptr(heap_base, global_pe)) + off;
186	    }
187	
188	    __device__ __forceinline__ void rendezvous(const ::sg::fused::GridBarrier& bar) const {
189	        bar.sync();                       // all CTAs of THIS GPU arrived
190	        if (blockIdx.x == 0) {            // one CTA crosses the GPU boundary
191	            // Drain THIS PE's outstanding symmetric stores so the ascending-pe
192	            // NVLink loads on every peer observe our published partial, THEN
193	            // join the TP-group barrier (team-scoped — not the whole world).
194	            nvshmem_quiet();
195	            nvshmemx_barrier_block(tp_team_);
196	        }
197	        bar.sync();                       // release every CTA after the cross-GPU join
198	    }
199	};
200	#endif  // SG_HAS_NVSHMEM
201	
202	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
203	//  tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order — THE all-reduce both transports share.
204	//
205	//  PRE: every PE has PUBLISHED its fp32 partial at symmetric offset `slot_off`
206	//  (length n) and the caller has crossed `tr.rendezvous(bar)` once (so all
207	//  publishes are visible). POST: `dst[i] = Σ_pe partial_pe[i]`, summed in
208	//  ASCENDING pe order in fp32 — bit-identical on every PE and across reruns
209	//  (design §5.2/§2.7: structural order, the A/A/A non-negotiable). The caller
210	//  crosses `tr.rendezvous(bar)` again before REUSING the slot.
211	//
212	//  `tid`/`nthreads` define this PE's cooperative element loop. In the loopback
213	//  every virtual PE redundantly computes its own copy (each PE strides its own
214	//  CTA group's threads) — exactly what real per-GPU ranks do.
215	//
216	//  This is deliberately NOT nvshmem_float_sum_reduce: that collective's
217	//  reduction order is unspecified ⇒ ULP drift run-to-run ⇒ A/A/A failure
218	//  (design §5.2). The hand-rolled ascending-pe loop IS the deliverable.
219	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
220	template <class Transport>
221	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order(
222	        const Transport& tr, int64_t slot_off, float* __restrict__ dst,
223	        int64_t n, int tid, int nthreads) {
224	    const int P = tr.n_pes();
225	    for (int64_t i = tid; i < n; i += nthreads) {
226	        float acc = 0.0f;
227	        #pragma unroll 1
228	        for (int pe = 0; pe < P; ++pe) {        // ASCENDING pe — fixed order
229	            acc += tr.peer(slot_off, pe)[i];
230	        }
231	        dst[i] = acc;
232	    }
233	}
234	
235	// Variant writing the reduced value back INTO this PE's symmetric slot (in-place
236	// consumers); same fixed order. Safe because every PE reads ALL peers before any
237	// PE can pass the post-reduce rendezvous the caller crosses before reuse — the
238	// read-before-overwrite hazard is what that second rendezvous exists for, so
239	// this variant must write to a DIFFERENT slot than it reads. Kept explicit:
240	template <class Transport>
241	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order_to_slot(
242	        const Transport& tr, int64_t src_slot_off, int64_t dst_slot_off,
243	        int64_t n, int tid, int nthreads) {
244	    float* dst = tr.local(dst_slot_off);
245	    tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order(tr, src_slot_off, dst, n, tid, nthreads);
246	}
247	
248	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
249	//  make_transport_from_comm<Par> — the ONE place that selects the transport
250	//  from a populated par::CommCtx, so the megakernel constructs `tr` with a
251	//  single call (no #if clutter at the call site). Returns:
252	//    * NvshmemTransport       when -DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM (the real 8×H100 path),
253	//    * LoopbackTransport      otherwise (the single-GPU honest simulation).
254	//  Both read the SAME CommCtx fields (sym-heap base, stride, team pe/size), so
255	//  the launcher populates ONE struct and either transport binds it. Only ever
256	//  called under `if constexpr (Par::kTPComm)` (folded away on SingleGPU), so it
257	//  is never instantiated on the byte-identical default path.
258	//
259	//  The CommCtx type is forward-declared opaquely here to avoid pulling
260	//  parallel_config.cuh's include into every tp_transport.cuh consumer; the real
261	//  definition (par::CommCtx) is included by the megakernel before this is used.
262	//  The fields read are POD (float*/int64_t/int) — no NVSHMEM type crosses the
263	//  CommCtx boundary (the team handle is a void* cast to nvshmem_team_t here).
264	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
265	template <class Par, class CommT>
266	__device__ __forceinline__ auto make_transport_from_comm(const CommT& comm) {
267	#if defined(SG_HAS_NVSHMEM)
268	    return NvshmemTransport{
269	        reinterpret_cast<float*>(comm.tp_sym_heap),
270	        static_cast<nvshmem_team_t>(reinterpret_cast<intptr_t>(comm.tp_comm_handle)),
271	        comm.tp_team_n_pes, comm.tp_team_local_pe };
272	#else
273	    return LoopbackTransport{
274	        reinterpret_cast<float*>(comm.tp_sym_heap), comm.tp_heap_stride_floats,
275	        comm.tp_team_n_pes, comm.tp_team_local_pe };
276	#endif
277	}
278	
279	}}}}  // namespace sg::fused::sm90::tp
280	
281	#endif  // SG_FUSED_SM90_TP_TRANSPORT_CUH_

156	    Y1_ref = torch.zeros(M * D, device=dev)
157	    dX_ref = torch.zeros(M * D, device=dev)
158	    dW0_ref = torch.zeros(DFF * D, device=dev)
159	    db0_ref = torch.zeros(DFF, device=dev)
160	    dW1_ref = torch.zeros(D * DFF, device=dev)
161	    db1_ref = torch.zeros(D, device=dev)
162	    Y1_ch = torch.zeros(M * D, device=dev)
163	    dX_ch = torch.zeros(M * D, device=dev)
164	    mod.tp_reference_run(P, X.to(dev), dY1.to(dev),
165	                         W0.to(dev), b0.to(dev), W1.to(dev), b1.to(dev),
166	                         W0s.to(dev), b0s.to(dev), W1s.to(dev),
167	                         Y1_ref, dX_ref, dW0_ref, db0_ref, dW1_ref, db1_ref,
168	                         Y1_ch, dX_ch)
169	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
170	
171	    # (c) transport-neutrality: TP result == serial chunked-order, BIT-EXACT.
172	    chunked = torch.equal(Y1v[0], Y1_ch) and torch.equal(dXv[0], dX_ch)
173	
174	    # (d) slice-exactness of the dW/db shards vs the UNSHARDED reference.
175	    #     col-parallel dW0/db0: rank r owns full rows [r*F,(r+1)*F) — the dense
176	    #     concat IS the full [DFF, D] in row order, so equality is direct.
177	    slice_w0 = torch.equal(dW0, dW0_ref)
178	    slice_b0 = torch.equal(db0, db0_ref)
179	    #     row-parallel dW1: rank r owns full cols [r*F,(r+1)*F); reassemble.
180	    dW1_re = torch.empty(D, DFF, device=dev)
181	    dW1v = dW1.view(P, D, F)
182	    for r in range(P):
183	        dW1_re[:, r * F:(r + 1) * F] = dW1v[r]
184	    slice_w1 = torch.equal(dW1_re.reshape(-1), dW1_ref)
185	    slice_b1 = torch.equal(db1v[0], db1_ref)
186	
187	    # (e) vs the unsharded full-K reference (chunk reassociation) — tol, report.
188	    def _rel(a, b):
189	        d = (a - b).abs().max().item()
190	        n = b.abs().max().item() + 1e-30
191	        return d, d / n
192	    dY1_abs, dY1_rel = _rel(Y1v[0], Y1_ref)
193	    dDX_abs, dDX_rel = _rel(dXv[0], dX_ref)
194	    parity = dY1_rel < _PARITY_TOL and dDX_rel < _PARITY_TOL
195	
196	    ok = aaa and cross and chunked and slice_w0 and slice_b0 and slice_w1 and slice_b1 and parity
197	    if verbose:
198	        print(f"  [TP={P}] (a) cross-rank bit-eq={cross} | (b) A/A/A={aaa} | "
199	              f"(c) ==chunked-serial={chunked} | (d) dW slices: W0={slice_w0} "
200	              f"b0={slice_b0} W1={slice_w1} b1={slice_b1} | "
201	              f"(e) vs unsharded: Y1 rel={dY1_rel:.3e} dX rel={dDX_rel:.3e} "
202	              f"(tol {_PARITY_TOL:.0e}) parity={parity}", flush=True)
203	    return ok, dict(aaa=aaa, cross=cross, chunked=chunked,
204	                    slice_w0=slice_w0, slice_b0=slice_b0, slice_w1=slice_w1,
205	                    slice_b1=slice_b1, parity=parity,
206	                    y1_rel=dY1_rel, dx_rel=dDX_rel)
207

209	_TP_DEGREES = [2, 4]

216	    transport-neutrality (bit-exact vs serial chunked-order) + dW slice-exactness

1	"""grokking_optimizers/parallel/shard_map.py — the ZeRO shard PARTITION.
2	
3	IMPLEMENTS /workspace/.parallelism_design.md §3.4 (the shard partition that
4	respects the per-TENSOR optimizer constraint) + the elementwise even-partition
5	helper (design §2.4 "shard the flat [0,total) by even-partition").
6	
7	THE PROBLEM (design §3.4): ``ZeRO3Sharder._even_partition`` splits the FLAT param
8	buffer mid-tensor. That breaks muon / SuperGrok11 / SuperGrok15 / SuperGrok2 —
9	their P2.x optimizer stages (Newton–Schulz over a whole 2D weight; the per-tensor
10	meta-net mu/gate; SG2's segmented sort + CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU) need the WHOLE
11	matrix/tensor on ONE rank (design §0.4/§2.4). So the ZeRO-3 shard for those cells
12	must be TENSOR-GRANULAR, not element-granular.
13	
14	THIS MODULE (pure functions on SIZE LISTS — no torch, no torch.distributed, no
15	GPU, so it is CPU/CI-testable per design §7):
16	
17	  * :func:`even_partition`            — the flat element partition (mirrors
18	                                        ``distributed._even_partition`` exactly).
19	  * :func:`partition_elementwise_even`— per-rank flat slices for the ELEMENTWISE
20	                                        optimizers (finer, best balance).
21	  * :func:`partition_tensor_granular` — assign WHOLE tensors to ranks (greedy by
22	                                        numel, balanced) so NO tensor is split —
23	                                        REQUIRED for muon/SG11/SG15/SG2 (§3.4).
24	  * :func:`shard_mode_for_optimizer`  — key the mode off the optimizer (§3.4:
25	                                        elementwise → flat-even; per-tensor →
26	                                        tensor-granular).
27	
28	It does NOT touch ``distributed.py``; a caller (e.g. a future
29	``fused_train_step_distributed``, design §6.2) picks the mode via
30	:func:`shard_mode_for_optimizer` and calls the matching partitioner.
31	"""
32	
33	from __future__ import annotations
34	
35	import dataclasses
36	from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple
37	
38	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
39	#  Optimizer → shard-mode taxonomy (design §0.4 / §2.4 / §3.4).
40	#
41	#  ELEMENTWISE: shard the flat [0,total) — every per-element update is local, so
42	#  splitting a tensor across ranks is fine. (grokadamw/looksam/prodigy are
43	#  elementwise at APPLY; their global scalar is handled by a tiny all-reduce, NOT
44	#  by the shard partition — so they shard elementwise here.)
45	#
46	#  PER-TENSOR: a whole matrix/tensor must live on one rank (the P2.x stage reads
47	#  the whole tensor cooperatively). muon is per-MATRIX (NS over each 2D weight);
48	#  SG11/SG15/SG2 are per-TENSOR (meta-net over each tensor's elements).
49	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
50	ELEMENTWISE_OPTIMIZERS = frozenset({
51	    "adamw", "lion", "grokfast", "grokadamw", "looksam", "prodigy", "neuralgrok",
52	})
53	PER_TENSOR_OPTIMIZERS = frozenset({
54	    "muon", "supergrok11", "supergrok15", "supergrok2",
55	})
56	
57	# OptId integers (mirror csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh::OptId) so a caller
58	# holding the numeric id can map to a mode too. Single source of the spelling.
59	_OPTID_TO_NAME: Dict[int, str] = {
60	    0: "adamw", 1: "lion", 2: "grokfast", 3: "grokadamw", 4: "looksam",
61	    5: "prodigy", 6: "neuralgrok", 7: "muon", 8: "supergrok11",
62	    9: "supergrok15", 10: "supergrok2",
63	}
64	
65	_MODE_ELEMENTWISE = "elementwise_even"
66	_MODE_TENSOR_GRANULAR = "tensor_granular"
67	
68	
69	def shard_mode_for_optimizer(opt) -> str:
70	    """Return the shard mode an optimizer requires (design §3.4).
71	
72	    ``opt`` may be the optimizer NAME (str, case-insensitive) or its OptId int
73	    (0..10). Per-tensor cells (muon/SG11/SG15/SG2) → ``"tensor_granular"``;
74	    everything else → ``"elementwise_even"``.
75	
76	    Raises ``ValueError`` for an unknown optimizer (loud, no silent default —
77	    same discipline as the kernel dispatch, design §1.3).
78	    """
79	    if isinstance(opt, int):
80	        if opt not in _OPTID_TO_NAME:
81	            raise ValueError(f"unknown OptId {opt!r} (expected 0..10)")
82	        name = _OPTID_TO_NAME[opt]
83	    else:
84	        name = str(opt).strip().lower()
85	    if name in PER_TENSOR_OPTIMIZERS:
86	        return _MODE_TENSOR_GRANULAR
87	    if name in ELEMENTWISE_OPTIMIZERS:
88	        return _MODE_ELEMENTWISE
89	    raise ValueError(
90	        f"unknown optimizer {opt!r} — not in the 11-optimizer taxonomy "
91	        f"(elementwise={sorted(ELEMENTWISE_OPTIMIZERS)}, "
92	        f"per_tensor={sorted(PER_TENSOR_OPTIMIZERS)})"
93	    )
94	
95	
96	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
97	#  Result types.
98	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
99	
100	
101	@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
102	class TensorPlacement:
103	    """One tensor's whole-tensor placement under tensor-granular sharding.
104	
105	    ``name``/``numel`` identify the tensor; ``rank`` is the DP rank that owns it
106	    in full (no split). Tensor-granular sharding emits one of these per tensor.
107	    """
108	
109	    name: str
110	    numel: int
111	    rank: int
112	
113	
114	@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
115	class ShardPlan:
116	    """A partition result: each rank's owned (name, start, end) flat slices.
117	
118	    ``slices[r]`` is the list of ``(name, start, end)`` slices rank ``r`` owns
119	    (``end`` exclusive, in the tensor's OWN flat index space). For tensor-granular
120	    mode every slice is a whole tensor ``(name, 0, numel)``; for elementwise mode
121	    a tensor may appear on several ranks as contiguous sub-slices.
122	
123	    ``mode`` is ``"elementwise_even"`` or ``"tensor_granular"``. ``rank_numel[r]``
124	    is the total element count rank ``r`` owns (the balance metric).
125	    """
126	
127	    mode: str
128	    world: int
129	    slices: List[List[Tuple[str, int, int]]]
130	    rank_numel: List[int]
131	
132	    @property
133	    def total_numel(self) -> int:
134	        return sum(self.rank_numel)
135	
136	    def imbalance(self) -> float:
137	        """max/mean rank load (1.0 == perfectly balanced; higher == lumpier).
138	
139	        Tensor-granular is necessarily lumpier than elementwise (whole tensors
140	        can't be split), so this is the "honest cost, measure it" number design
141	        §3.4 calls for. Returns 1.0 for the degenerate world<=1.
142	        """
143	        if self.world <= 1 or self.total_numel == 0:
144	            return 1.0
145	        mean = self.total_numel / self.world
146	        return max(self.rank_numel) / mean if mean > 0 else 1.0
147	
148	
149	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
150	#  Elementwise flat partition (design §2.4).
151	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
152	
153	
154	def even_partition(numel: int, world: int, rank: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
155	    """Contiguous, padded-even partition of ``numel`` across ``world`` ranks.
156	
157	    Byte-for-byte the convention of ``distributed._even_partition`` (the
158	    DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 flat-partition): each rank owns ``ceil(numel/world)``
159	    elements (last rank clamped), so the union covers ``[0, numel)`` exactly with
160	    no overlap. Mirrored here (not imported) so this pure-Python module needs no
161	    torch import; a unit test asserts it agrees with ``distributed`` when torch
162	    is present.
163	    """
164	    if world <= 1:
165	        return 0, numel
166	    per = (numel + world - 1) // world
167	    start = min(rank * per, numel)
168	    end = min(start + per, numel)
169	    return start, end
170	
171	
172	def partition_elementwise_even(
173	    named_sizes: Sequence[Tuple[str, int]], world: int
174	) -> ShardPlan:
175	    """ELEMENTWISE shard: split each tensor's flat buffer evenly across ranks.
176	
177	    The finer partition (design §2.4) — best balance, valid for the elementwise
178	    optimizers (adamw/lion/grokfast/neuralgrok + the elementwise core of
179	    grokadamw/looksam/prodigy). A tensor MAY be split across ranks (that's fine:
180	    every per-element apply is local).
181	
182	    ``named_sizes`` is ``[(name, numel), ...]`` (e.g. from ``named_parameters()``
183	    sizes). Returns a :class:`ShardPlan` in ``"elementwise_even"`` mode.
184	    """
185	    world = max(1, int(world))
186	    slices: List[List[Tuple[str, int, int]]] = [[] for _ in range(world)]
187	    rank_numel = [0] * world
188	    for name, numel in named_sizes:
189	        numel = int(numel)
190	        if numel < 0:
191	            raise ValueError(f"tensor {name!r} has negative numel {numel}")
192	        for r in range(world):
193	            s, e = even_partition(numel, world, r)
194	            if e > s:
195	                slices[r].append((name, s, e))
196	                rank_numel[r] += e - s
197	    return ShardPlan(_MODE_ELEMENTWISE, world, slices, rank_numel)
198	
199	
200	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
201	#  Tensor-granular partition (design §3.4) — the new requirement.
202	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
203	
204	
205	def partition_tensor_granular(
206	    named_sizes: Sequence[Tuple[str, int]], world: int
207	) -> ShardPlan:
208	    """Assign WHOLE tensors to ranks (greedy by numel, balanced) — design §3.4.
209	
210	    No tensor is split across ranks, which is REQUIRED for the per-tensor
211	    optimizers (muon/SuperGrok11/SuperGrok15/SuperGrok2): their P2.x stages need
212	    the whole matrix/tensor on one rank (design §0.4/§2.4), and the co-located
213	    optimizer state (m/mu/sharpness/slow/gru_state) rides with its tensor.
214	
215	    ALGORITHM — greedy longest-processing-time (LPT): sort tensors descending by
216	    numel, then assign each to the currently least-loaded rank. This is the
217	    standard balanced whole-item bin-packing heuristic; it is deterministic
218	    (a pure function of the size list + world — design §2.7 requires deterministic
219	    shard boundaries) and gives a good (not optimal) balance. Ties broken by the
220	    lowest rank index, then by tensor name, so the result is stable across runs.
221	
222	    Balance is necessarily lumpier than elementwise (the embedding + ff matrices
223	    dominate), so :meth:`ShardPlan.imbalance` is the honest DP-efficiency cost
224	    design §3.4 says to measure.
225	
226	    ``named_sizes`` is ``[(name, numel), ...]``. Returns a :class:`ShardPlan` in
227	    ``"tensor_granular"`` mode where every owned slice is a whole tensor
228	    ``(name, 0, numel)``.
229	    """
230	    world = max(1, int(world))
231	    slices: List[List[Tuple[str, int, int]]] = [[] for _ in range(world)]
232	    rank_numel = [0] * world
233	
234	    # Validate + materialize.
235	    tensors: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
236	    for name, numel in named_sizes:
237	        numel = int(numel)
238	        if numel < 0:
239	            raise ValueError(f"tensor {name!r} has negative numel {numel}")
240	        tensors.append((name, numel))
241	
242	    # LPT: descending by numel; tie-break by name so the order is total + stable.
243	    order = sorted(tensors, key=lambda t: (-t[1], t[0]))
244	    for name, numel in order:
245	        # Least-loaded rank; ties → lowest rank index (min() is stable on the
246	        # (load, rank) key).
247	        r = min(range(world), key=lambda k: (rank_numel[k], k))
248	        slices[r].append((name, 0, numel))
249	        rank_numel[r] += numel
250	
251	    # Keep each rank's slice list in the input (named_parameters()) order, so the
252	    # owned slices are reported in a stable, layout-meaningful order (the kernel
253	    # addresses tensors in named_parameters() order — decoder_layout.cuh).
254	    input_order = {name: i for i, (name, _) in enumerate(tensors)}
255	    for r in range(world):
256	        slices[r].sort(key=lambda sl: input_order[sl[0]])
257	
258	    return ShardPlan(_MODE_TENSOR_GRANULAR, world, slices, rank_numel)
259	
260	
261	def partition_for_optimizer(
262	    named_sizes: Sequence[Tuple[str, int]], world: int, opt
263	) -> ShardPlan:
264	    """Pick the partition mode from the optimizer (design §3.4) and run it.
265	
266	    Convenience wrapper: per-tensor cells → :func:`partition_tensor_granular`;
267	    elementwise cells → :func:`partition_elementwise_even`.
268	    """
269	    mode = shard_mode_for_optimizer(opt)
270	    if mode == _MODE_TENSOR_GRANULAR:
271	        return partition_tensor_granular(named_sizes, world)
272	    return partition_elementwise_even(named_sizes, world)
